items.title: Iranians face 50th day of internet blackout as ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Ceasefire brings some relief for Iranians but economic outlook ...

items.description: As a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran inches toward its April 22 expiration, Iranians are navigating a precarious existence shaped by weeks of aerial bombardment, a brutal government crackdown on mass protests, and an economic crisis with no clear end in sight. The pause in fighting has brought a measure of relief — but for many, it has also sharpened fears that the worst may still lie ahead.

items.title: Iranians fear regime will tighten grip once ceasefire holds

featured_image.name: Military Parade Of Iran's SelfSacrificing Daughters

items.description:
Iranians struggling to piece together daily life after weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes and a brutal crackdown on protesters are gripped by fear that conditions will only worsen once the guns fall silent, even as a fragile ceasefire offers a momentary reprieve.

"The war will end, but that's when our real problems with the system begin," a 37-year-old named Fariba who took part in the January unrest told Reuters by phone from Iran. "I'm very afraid that if the regime reaches an agreement with the United States, it will increase pressure on ordinary people."[1]

items.title: Iran's 'mosquito fleet' holds Hormuz despite 155 warships sunk

featured_image.name: Why Iran has a speedboat swarm that's punching above its ...

items.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, U.S. and allied strikes have sunk more than 155 Iranian naval vessels and wiped out entire classes of warships. Yet the fleet Tehran relies on most to control the Strait of Hormuz — a sprawling armada of small, fast boats operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps — remains largely intact and continues to menace one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Australia, Japan sign $7B stealth frigate deal

featured_image.name: Australia to seek deal with Japan in frigate development talks

items.description: Australia and Japan on Saturday signed contracts launching a A$10 billion (US$7 billion) deal to supply Australia with advanced stealth frigates, in what has been described as Japan's most consequential defense export agreement since World War II.[1][2]

items.title: China reaches 125 GW to become world's largest nuclear power

featured_image.name: Phase 1 of world's largest nuclear power base goes live in China

items.description: China has claimed the top spot globally for total installed nuclear power capacity, reaching 125 gigawatts, according to a blue book released Friday by the China Nuclear Energy Association. The milestone underscores Beijing's accelerating push to expand its atomic energy fleet at a pace unmatched by any other nation.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver

featured_image.name: Trump ups sanctions on Russian oil

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.[1][2]

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.[2]

items.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza

featured_image.name: UNICEF says Israeli fire kills two Gaza water truck drivers ...

items.description: UNICEF said Friday it was "outraged" after two truck drivers it contracted to deliver clean water to families in the Gaza Strip were killed by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. Two others were injured in the incident, which occurred during routine water trucking operations early Friday morning, according to the agency's statement.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israeli drone kills one in southern Lebanon hours into ceasefire

featured_image.name: Israeli drone attack kills 1 in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire deal

items.description:
An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in southern Lebanon on Friday, killing one person on the first full day of a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire, even as President Trump declared on social media that Israel was "PROHIBITED" from bombing Lebanon.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that a motorcyclist was killed in the town of Kounine, in the Bint Jbeil district, after being targeted by an Israeli drone. The Lebanese army reported additional violations on Friday morning, including intermittent shelling of several southern villages and firing on an ambulance team in Kounine.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran threatens to reclose Strait of Hormuz if US blockade continues

featured_image.name: Ships crossing Hormuz need OK from IRGC, unfreezing funds ...

items.description: Hours after declaring the Strait of Hormuz fully reopened to commercial shipping, Iran warned on Friday that it could shut the waterway again if the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

items.title: Iran's buried Pickaxe Mountain site looms over nuclear talks

featured_image.name: Inside Iran's top secret 'nuclear energy mountain'

items.description: As the United States and Iran inch toward a possible deal ahead of the April 22 ceasefire deadline, a deeply buried nuclear facility near Natanz known as Pickaxe Mountain has emerged as one of the most contentious obstacles to any lasting agreement — and some analysts and Iran hawks are pressing President Trump to consider extreme measures to destroy it.

items.title: Pakistan deployed fighter jets to escort Iran delegation home from talks

featured_image.name: Pakistani jets escorted Iranian delegation back home amid ...

items.description:
Pakistan's air force mounted a large-scale aerial operation to escort Iranian negotiators back from inconclusive peace talks in Islamabad, deploying around two dozen fighter jets and an airborne warning and control system after Iranian officials raised the possibility they could be targeted by Israel, Reuters reported exclusively on Friday.[1]

The escort mission, which took place on Sunday following the collapse of the first round of US-Iran proximity talks, underscored the extreme security risks surrounding the highest-level engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

items.title: UNICEF reports 172 children killed as Lebanon ceasefire takes effect

featured_image.name: The impact of conflict on Lebanon's children - UNICEF Australia

items.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight local time on April 17, offering a fragile pause in hostilities after 46 days of renewed war that has killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over one million. As the guns fell quiet, UNICEF reported that at least 172 children had been killed and 661 injured since fighting resumed on March 2, with more than 415,000 children forced from their homes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran denies agreeing to hand enriched uranium to US

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday flatly denied President Trump's assertion that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium to the United States, exposing a sharp public rift in fragile nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

"Iran's enriched uranium is not going to be transferred anywhere," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television. He added that the "transfer of Iran's enriched uranium to the US has never been raised in negotiations".[1][2][3]

The denial came hours after Trump told CBS News in a phone interview that Iran had "agreed to everything," including a joint operation to retrieve the country's roughly 2,000 kilograms of enriched uranium and bring it to American soil. "Our people, together with the Iranians, are going to work together to go get it. And then we'll take it to the United States," Trump said, adding that no U.S. troops would be involved.[4][5]

items.title: Trump says US has 'prohibited' Israel from bombing Lebanon

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Strait of Hormuz open ‘for remaining period of ceasefire’

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Friday that the United States has banned Israel from conducting further airstrikes in Lebanon, issuing his strongest public directive yet to constrain Israeli military operations as a fragile 10-day ceasefire between the two countries enters its first full day.

"Israel will not be bombing Lebanon any longer. They are PROHIBITED from doing so by the USA. Enough is enough," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The statement came as part of a broader post in which Trump also pushed back against Iran's efforts to link the Lebanon truce to ongoing U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations. "This deal is in no way subject to Lebanon, either, but the USA will, separately, work with Lebanon, and deal with the Hezboolah situation in an appropriate manner," he wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says US will recover enriched uranium from Iran

featured_image.name: Trump holds situation room meeting on Iran nuclear deal ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States plans to work jointly with Iran to recover its stockpile of enriched uranium and transport it to the US, describing the effort as a gradual process that would begin soon.

"We're going to get it together. We're going to go in with Iran, at a nice leisurely pace, and go down and start excavating with big machinery… We'll bring it back to the United States," Trump told Reuters in a phone interview. He said what he called "nuclear dust" would be retrieved "very soon," referring to enriched uranium believed to remain underground after US and Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities at Fordow and Natanz in June 2025.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says Iran “agreed to everything” in war talks

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran has agreed to hand over enriched uranium

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that Iran has "agreed to everything" in negotiations to end the weeks-long war between the two nations, claiming Tehran will surrender its enriched uranium stockpile and indefinitely suspend its nuclear program. Iran has not confirmed any such agreement.

items.title: Breeding top 1-5% of corals could boost reef survival, study finds

featured_image.name: Darwin in a lab: Coral evolution tweaked for global warming ...

items.description: A pair of studies published this week by an international team of coral scientists delivers both a warning and a roadmap: assisted evolution can help corals survive worsening marine heatwaves, but only if the research accelerates and selection is far more aggressive than anything tried so far.

items.title: Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz amid ceasefire as jet fuel crisis grips Europe

featured_image.name: Jet fuel shortage: Why Iran war could ground flights in Europe

items.description: Europe has roughly six weeks of jet fuel remaining, the head of the International Energy Agency warned on Thursday, raising the prospect of widespread flight cancellations just as the continent's peak summer travel season approaches. The warning came as the nearly seven-week closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke off a critical supply route for global energy.

items.title: Trump says Iran agreed to indefinitely suspend nuclear program; Tehran denies it

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description: President Donald Trump declared on Friday that Iran has agreed to suspend its nuclear program indefinitely, claiming a deal to end the war that has engulfed the Middle East since late February is "mostly complete." In a phone interview with Bloomberg, Trump said Tehran would not receive any frozen U.S. funds in exchange for the suspension and that talks toward a final agreement would likely resume over the weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan.[1][2]

items.title: Iran war reshapes global energy policy as nations fast-track renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war: A global energy shock could accelerate a shift to renewables

items.description:
The escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — is reshaping global energy policy, as countries exposed to the largest oil supply disruption in decades accelerate their pivot toward renewable power.

Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas supply transits, has locked an estimated 13 million barrels of oil per day out of global markets. A U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports, ordered by President Donald Trump on Monday after ceasefire talks collapsed, has further choked the waterway. The twin disruptions have pushed crude prices near historic highs and laid bare the vulnerabilities of fossil fuel dependency.[1][2][3]
